MRK.rationale: MRK's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe earnings collapse: net income swung to -$4.24B (EPS -$1.72) from +$5.79B in Q3 2025, driven by a massive operating loss of -$3.53B despite revenue of $16.29B. This is not a one-off — the operating margin collapsed from ~39% in Q3 2025 to -21.7% in Q1 2026, suggesting a large impairment, restructuring charge, or acquisition-related cost. Meanwhile, the stock has surged 57% over the past year to $125.45, pushing the P/E to 34.7x — the highest in the 12-month window (range 11.1–34.7) — on what appears to be a deeply impaired earnings base. The P/B of 6.75x is also at the top of its 4.0–6.8 range. Forward guidance of $5.04–$5.16 EPS for 2026 implies a forward P/E of ~24–25x, which is still elevated for a company facing Keytruda patent cliff in 2028–2029, Gardasil demand weakness in China/Japan, and recent oncology pipeline setbacks (EVOKE-03 discontinuation, LITESPARK-012 miss). The CMS proposed drug price negotiations starting 2029 add further structural headwinds. While the company has a diversified pipeline and strong cash generation ($3.92B operating cash flow in Q1), the combination of deteriorating near trajectory, extreme valuation vs. history, and multiple near-term risk catalysts (pipeline disappointments, regulatory pressure) makes this a strongly unattractive setup.

Gardasil vaccine sales declining in key international markets such as China and Japan due to weak demand trends
